issues.issue: Does s 14(6) of the Citizenship Act oust the Federal Court of Appeal's jurisdiction over the Federal Court's interlocutory motion ruling?
issues.applicant_position: Section 14(6) applies only to decisions on the ultimate citizenship question, so the motion ruling is appealable.
issues.result_quote: Accordingly, in my opinion, this Court has jurisdiction to entertain the Minister’s appeal

issues.issue: Did the Motions Judge err in not striking the appeal as out of time under s 14(5)(b)?
issues.applicant_position: The 60-day limit runs from the date notice was mailed, not from receipt, so the appeal was late.
issues.respondent_position: Time should run from when the representative learned of the decision, so the appeal was not prejudiced and was timely.
issues.result_quote: the plain meaning of paragraph 14(3)(b) is that when notice is mailed, as it was here, the 60 day period starts at the date of mailing
